the hard- thermal-loop perturbation theory is a gauge invariant reorganization of QED at high temperature, that it is a systematic expansion for any coupling constant e, and that it provides a convergent expansion for the thermodynamic potentials of a hot QED gas.

the hard- thermal- loop perturbation reorganization of QED thermodynamics improves the convergence of successive approximations to free energy at large couplings, e~2, and that the reorganization is gauge- invariant by construction.
HTLpt improves the convergence of successive approximations to thermodynamic quantities in QED, and that the three-loop HTLpt thermodynamic potential is completely analytic.

the thermodynamic properties of a hot gas of massless electrons and photons, in particular, the free energy and the equation of state.
the study of the weakly coupled thermodynamics of QED.

the HTLpt resummation is a useful tool for the calculation of thermodynamic quantities in the weak-coupling regime.
the HTLpt reorganization of the weak-coupling perturbation series is an important and necessary step for obtaining accurate thermodynamic results at large coupling.

the HTLpt reorganization is a systematic procedure for improving the convergence of the perturbation theory for thermodynamic functions.
